title: DOJ folds Apple-Siri Gemini payments into Google search-remedies case by Q1 2027
body: Apple's WWDC concession that the rebuilt Siri runs on a custom ~1.2-trillion-parameter Google Gemini model, for roughly $1 billion a year, layers a second multi-billion-dollar commercial tie on top of the existing search-default payment Google already makes Apple. That earlier payment is the exact conduct at the center of the DOJ's monopolization case against Google: the court found the default-search deals unlawfully entrenched Google's dominance, and the remedies phase is still live, with Google appealing and the parties contesting how far behavioral fixes must reach. The new Siri arrangement gives the DOJ and the states a fresh, concrete data point that the two firms' entanglement is widening rather than unwinding precisely while a remedy is being designed. Expect the Antitrust Division to cite the Gemini-for-Siri deal in a post-trial remedies brief, a compliance-monitoring submission, or a new or amended civil investigative demand by the end of Q1 2027 - arguing that any decree limiting Google-Apple value transfer must reach the AI-assistant layer, not just search distribution, and treating the assistant slot as a second default that can foreclose rivals. The trigger is a formal filing or CID naming the Siri-Gemini payments; absent that on the docket by March 31, 2027, the prediction fails.

reasoning.because: Live DOJ Google remedies phase already targets Google-Apple default-search payments
reasoning.given: WWDC adds a ~$1B/yr Gemini-for-Siri tie on top of the same Google-Apple money flow
reasoning.so_that: Antitrust enforcers extend the remedy theory from search distribution to the AI-assistant default layer
reasoning.landing: By Q1 2027, DOJ filing or CID naming the Siri-Gemini payments
reasoning.plain_language: Two companies already in court for paying each other now pay each other more, so regulators look harder.

summary: Apple's $1B/yr Gemini-for-Siri deal adds a second Google payment atop the search-default ties already central to the DOJ's live Google monopoly case. Expect the DOJ or state AGs to cite it in a remedies brief or civil investigative demand by Q1 2027.
